meetings.headline: Committee voted a records-storage position paper and drafted three building-use scenarios for town offices.
meetings.summary: The committee edited and approved a position paper urging departments to digitize or store records off-site to minimize costly storage space in any new or remodeled building. It then worked through three draft scenarios for town offices, community use, TC Passios, Ritter, Town Hall, Brooks House and 30 School Street. It also approved prior minutes and set upcoming meeting dates.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously by roll call to approve a position paper urging departments to digitize or store records off-site rather than in costly new building space.
The chair will email the approved paper to members for sharing with appointing boards, and departments are asked to reply by September 30.
Members drafted three building-use scenarios for town offices, covering TC Passios, Ritter, Town Hall, the Brooks House and 30 School Street.
The three scenarios will be reported to the select board, which decides which options go to town meeting; no November warrant article will be sought.
The chair may ask the board for ARPA funding for a structural analysis of buildings, and meetings were set for September 19, October 3 and October 17.

why_it_matters: How much records space any new or remodeled town building must include affects its size and cost, and so what residents may later be asked to vote on at town meeting.
The committee will not bring a warrant article in November, so a building plan for town offices is a later vote, and the select board decides which options reach it.
